task.description: Idiom/scope gate on REQ-230's three-layer SQL-injection defence (Types/Allowlist/Compiler), independently re-run rather than trusting ELIXIR-DEV's or SECURITY-REVIEWER's handoffs: re-ran mix compile/format/test myself, re-read all three modules and the test file line by line against the validated design, checked design fidelity, AC-to-test mapping, the flagged String.to_existing_atom/1 precedent, SECURITY-REVIEWER's ILIKE-escaping observation, scope via git diff --stat, and OTP/layering idiom against REQ-227's Record.Validator precedent.

result.note:
1) Own runs, all green: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean (no output, no warnings). `mix format --check-formatted` clean. `mix test test/letflow/entities/query_test.exs` -> 26 tests, 0 failures, 26.5s. `mix test test/letflow/entities/` (full regression) -> 129 tests, 0 failures, 84.6s -- matches both prior handoffs' counts, independently reproduced.

2) Design fidelity: module names/paths exactly match design section 3.1 -- Letflow.Entities.Query.Types (lib/letflow/entities/query/types.ex), .Allowlist (allowlist.ex), .Compiler (compiler.ex). filter_op()/sort_dir() closed unions match section 2.1's tables exactly (12 filter ops, 2 sort dirs), parse_filter_op/1 and parse_sort_dir/1 are plain exhaustive case statements with a catch-all {:error,{:unknown_operator/unknown_sort_dir, raw}} clause -- no regex, no atom conversion of caller input (types.ex:81-112). Allowlist.load/2's step order matches section 3.3 exactly (tenant-schema validation -> get_active_definition_by_name -> decode -> typed-column-then-json-field build -> merge with typed_column_entries as override). The shadowing rule (Map.merge(json_field_entries, typed_column_entries), typed-column wins) is implemented exactly as section 3.4 specifies and is restated verbatim in Allowlist's moduledoc (verified by reading allowlist.ex:13-27, and independently by AC3's own moduledoc test at query_test.exs:239-244). Compiler.compile/2's step order (allowlist load -> per-filter value-arity/field-resolve/type-check/build -> AND-fold -> per-sort resolve/build -> assemble) matches design section 5.1 exactly. The fragment/1 dispatch shape matches section 5.2 precisely: six module-attribute literals (@string_fragment .. @datetime_fragment, compiler.ex:225-230), each a fixed compile-time binary, selected by pattern-matching json_cast_dynamic/2 on the closed field_type() atom, with r.field_values and ^field_name as the two fragment placeholders and ^value as a further separate bound parameter -- confirmed no fragment call anywhere builds its literal via interpolation/concatenation.

3) All 7 ACs have genuine tests, verified by reading query_test.exs directly against REQ-230's literal AC text in docs/requirements.yaml lines 14016-14022: AC1 ('operator outside the closed enum ... rejected ... with a specific error identifying the unrecognised operator') -> describe 'AC1' tests at query_test.exs:138-182, including one using an actual SQL-injection-shaped string as the bogus operator (line 179). AC2 ('field name absent from the allowlist ... rejected before reaching the compiler ... plausible-looking but non-existent field') -> describe 'AC2' at 189-229, four tests covering resolve_field/2 directly, a filter clause, a sort clause, and an unknown entity_type. AC3 ('typed column vs JSONB shadowing ... precedence rule stated explicitly in the moduledoc') -> describe 'AC3' at 238-305, five tests including a direct Code.fetch_docs/1 assertion on the moduledoc text (239-244) and the actual colliding-'deleted'-field scenario (246-267). AC4 ('every caller-supplied filter VALUE ... bound as a positional parameter ... demonstrated by a fixture containing a value with a SQL-metacharacter payload ... treated as inert data ... when the compiled query runs') -> describe 'AC4' at 314-426, four tests executed against real, sandboxed Postgres (not mocked) -- the DROP-TABLE-payload test (315-344) asserts Repo.aggregate count is unchanged before/after, which is a genuine non-tautological proof (a real DROP TABLE succeeding would make the aggregate raise Postgrex.Error(undefined_table) instead of returning 2). AC5 ('SECURITY-REVIEWER's hard gate is applied ... since it is a tenant-data query path') -> satisfied procedurally (this requirement in fact routed through and passed SECURITY-REVIEWER, handoff step-02b, PASS) and describe 'AC5' at 434-500 supplies the concrete material that gate used (full error-taxonomy test at 435-476, cross-tenant-isolation test at 478-500). AC6 ('no route or controller file is added or modified') -> git diff --stat (below) confirms structurally, and describe 'AC6' at 510-516 pins the module namespace as non-Plug. AC7 ('mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted') -> satisfied by my own independent run in item 1.

4) The flagged String.to_existing_atom/1 discrepancy: confirmed reasonable and precedent-following, not a new problem. Read lib/letflow/entities/records.ex:406-417 -- Letflow.Entities.Records's own private definition_document/1/field_document/1 does the exact same thing: String.to_existing_atom(Map.fetch!(field, "type")) on the JSON-decoded, string-keyed field map. Allowlist.load/2's private field_document/1 (allowlist.ex:167-174) is a direct structural copy of that established idiom, with its own comment citing the precedent and explaining why it's safe (the full closed set of Definition.field_type() atoms is already compiled into the codebase, so String.to_existing_atom/1 cannot raise on any value definition-creation-time validation would have accepted). Not scope creep, not a new pattern -- reuse of an existing, already-reviewed workaround for a real design-doc gap Records's own moduledoc already names.

5) SECURITY-REVIEWER's ILIKE wildcard-escaping observation: assessed and accepted as non-blocking, matching SECURITY-REVIEWER's own characterization. Checked whether this is a regression against an established convention or a genuinely new gap: lib/letflow/definitions.ex:1922-1926's existing where_name/2 (the codebase's only pre-existing ILIKE precedent, cited by the design itself in section 0/5.3) has the identical property -- it builds "%" <> name <> "%" and passes it as one bound ^pattern parameter without escaping literal % or _ in the caller-supplied name either. The new compiler's :contains/:starts_with handling (compiler.ex:204-212, 296-306) is therefore consistent with, not a regression from, this codebase's one existing ILIKE convention -- it is a pre-existing repo-wide query-precision characteristic, not something this diff introduced or worsened. Given SECURITY-REVIEWER's own finding that no security invariant is affected (the wildcard-broadening effect stays entirely inside the already-tenant-scoped, already-authorized query), and the pattern being identical to lib/letflow/definitions.ex's existing behaviour, I am not filing this under docs/issues/ -- it is a cosmetic precision nit shared by two modules, not a class of invalid state a type change could prevent, and not a newly-introduced defect. If a future requirement wants LIKE-special-character escaping as a real feature, it would apply symmetrically to where_name/2 too, which is out of this requirement's scope.

6) Scope discipline: `git diff 0f5710f8..HEAD --stat` (run myself) shows exactly 12 files: 7 handoff/design-bookkeeping JSON files under handoffs/WF02-REQ230-20260907/ (step-00 through step-02b), the validated design doc (lib/letflow/design/req230-entity-query-dsl-compiler.md), the three new library modules (types.ex/allowlist.ex/compiler.ex), and the one test file (query_test.exs) -- 2,336 insertions, 0 deletions, no other file touched. No lib/letflow_web/** path, no router/controller file, no cursor-pagination or field-grant-redaction code (REQ-231's scope) anywhere in the diff -- confirmed both by the file list and by reading compiler.ex end-to-end (no LIMIT/keyset where, no field-grant/redaction logic).

7) IDIOM/OTP: no unnecessary process machinery anywhere in this diff -- all three modules are plain, stateless (Types) or read-then-return (Allowlist/Compiler) library functions; compile/2 explicitly never calls Repo.* itself, matching the design's and the codebase's established 'compiler returns an unexecuted Ecto.Query.t(), caller executes' posture. The closed-enum/allowlist/compiler three-way split matches this codebase's established layering convention directly: compared against Letflow.Entities.Record.Validator's REQ-227 validate-before-use pattern (lib/letflow/entities/record/validator.ex) -- both follow the same shape of 'reshape/derive from a REQ-225 definition, then delegate the actual check/build to a narrowly-scoped function, with a clearly named rejection point and typed {:ok,_}/{:error,_} tuples throughout, no bare pattern matches on external input'. No abstraction (behaviour, macro, generic plumbing) appears ahead of what this requirement's scope needs -- the three-module split is justified in the design (section 3.1) by genuinely distinct call-time inputs and failure domains (Types is pure, Allowlist needs prefix+DB, Compiler needs a loaded allowlist), not introduced speculatively; no REQ-231-scoped abstraction (cursor codec, field-grant loader) leaks into this diff. No type-safety gap found that a struct/Ecto.Enum change would newly close beyond what design section 9 already flags as open questions (case-sensitivity of :eq/:neq, :in/:not_in-against-JSONB fragment composition) -- both are already explicitly documented as accepted, deliberate design decisions rather than silent gaps, so no new docs/issues/ filing is warranted for this diff.

No BLOCKER, no scope creep, no idiom violation found. PASS.
